Accumulating positive emotions includes short-term pleasant experiences and longer-term steps toward values and priorities.

## Accumulating Positive Emotions {#accumulating-positive-emotions}

### Short Term

Do pleasant things that are possible now. Build positive events into each day, let small opportunities count, be mindful of pleasant experiences without multitasking, and return attention when worry pulls you away.

### Long Term

Make changes that increase positive events over time and support a life worth living:

1. Identify values that matter to you.
2. Choose one value to work on now.
3. Identify a few goals connected with that value.
4. Choose one goal and identify small action steps.
5. Take one step now and continue with the next effective step.

### Pleasant Events List

The three visual handouts below contain the full 225-item source list. Their native text versions make those activities searchable and readable with browser Find. The Pleasant Event Planner uses the same 225 source activities; no missing entries were found during this pass.

## Build Mastery {#build-mastery}

Continue with [Building Mastery & Cope Ahead](positive-emotions-mastery-cope-ahead.qmd#build-mastery).

## Cope Ahead {#cope-ahead}

Continue with [Building Mastery & Cope Ahead](positive-emotions-mastery-cope-ahead.qmd#cope-ahead).

## Treat Physical Illness {#treat-physical-illness}

Attend to physical illness, take prescribed medication, and arrange medical care when needed.

## Balanced Eating {#balanced-eating}

Eat regularly and in a balanced way so hunger, restriction, or extremes do not add avoidable vulnerability to emotion mind.

## Avoid Mood-Altering Substances {#avoid-mood-altering-substances}

Avoid non-prescribed mood-altering substances and use prescribed medications as directed.

## Balanced Sleep {#balanced-sleep}

Aim for the amount of sleep that helps you function and keep sleep timing as consistent as practical.

## Exercise {#exercise}

Use regular activity that fits your health and ability to support mood and reduce vulnerability.

#### Text Version

*Emotion Regulation Handout 15 (Emotion Regulation Worksheets 9, 10, 13)*

accumulate positive emotions in the short term by doing these things.

##### Build Positive Experiences noW

- INCREASE PLEASANT EVENTS that lead to positive emotions.

- Do ONE THING each day from the Pleasant Events List.

##### (See Emotion Regulation Handout 16.)

- Practice opposite action; AVOID AVOIDING.

- BE MINDFUL of pleasant events (no multitasking).

##### Be Mindful of Positive Experiences

- FOCUS your attention on positive moments when they are happening. No multitasking.

- REFOCUS your attention when your mind wanders to the negative.

- PARTICIPATE and ENGAGE fully in each experience.

##### Be Unmindful of Worries

Such as . . .

- When the positive experience will end.

- Whether you deserve this positive experience.

- How much more might be expected of you now.

#### Text Version

*Emotion Regulation Handout 17 (Emotion Regulation Worksheets 9, 11-11b, 13)*

Accumulate positive emotions in the long term to build a “life worth living.” That is, make changes in your life so that positive events will occur in the future. Step 1. avoid avoiding. Start now to do what is needed to build the life you want. If you are not sure about what to do, follow the steps below. Step 2. identify values that are important to you.

**ASK: What values are really important to me in my life?**

Examples: Be productive; be part of a group; treat others well; be physically fit. Step 3. identify one value to work on now.

**ASK: What is really important to me, right now, to work on in my life?**

Example: Be productive. Step 4. identify a few goals related to this value.

**ASK: What specific goals can I work on that will make this value part of my life?**

Examples: Get a job where I can do something useful. Be more active keeping up with important tasks at home. Find a volunteer job that will use skills I already have. Step 5. choose one goal to work on now. Do pros and cons, if necessary, to select a goal to work on now. Example: Get a job where I can do something useful. Step 6. identify small action steps toward your goal.

**ASK: What small steps can I take to get to my goal?**

Examples: Visit places and look for job openings on the Internet in my area. Submit applications for jobs at places I want to work. Write résumé. Check out benefits at places I might want to work. Step 7. Take one action step now. Example: Go on Internet and check for jobs in my area.

<!-- native-resource-content:emotion-regulation-p062:end -->
